card.occupation: Part-time domiciliary care worker, doing about 12 hours a week of morning calls (washing, dressing, breakfasts, medication prompts) for an agency covering Sittingbourne and the villages towards Faversham
card.education_detail: Left school in the Netherlands at 16 with a MAVO certificate (roughly GCSE level). Did shop and cleaning work in her twenties after moving to England. Completed an NVQ Level 2 in Health and Social Care through the agency in her late forties, plus the usual mandatory refreshers in manual handling, safeguarding and medication.
card.household: Lives with her husband Keith, 67, a retired forklift driver who worked at a paper mill and then a distribution warehouse. They own a 1960s semi with a small back garden. Their two grown-up children have moved out: a son in Maidstone and a daughter in Rochester. There are three grandchildren, and they see them most weekends.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in a small town near Arnhem in the Netherlands. She met Keith on a coach holiday when she was 21 and moved to Kent in 1983. She has now lived in England for over forty years and thinks of herself as 'Dutch but been here forever'. Her parents have died, and she has a sister still in Gelderland whom she phones every Sunday. She was brought up loosely Protestant but drifted from it. Since her thirties she has gone to a small Spiritualist church in the town, mainly to the Sunday evening services and the occasional healing night. It came out of a friend taking her along after her mum died. She doesn't push it on anyone and calls it 'my church' without much explanation.
card.professional_persona: Reliable on the rota but not a planner. She does the same round of four or five regulars most weeks and is good with them: chatty, patient, unflappable with people who are confused or grumpy. Her paperwork in the care app is the weak spot, and the office sometimes chases her for incomplete notes. She doesn't want more hours or to move into senior carer work. She likes finishing by eleven and having the rest of the day.
card.sports_persona: Doesn't do any sport as such. She walks a fair bit for work and with her sister's old habit of cycling she still has a bike in the shed, but it hasn't been out in years. Keith watches the football, and she'll sit in the room with it on. She sometimes watches the speed skating if there's Dutch interest at the Winter Olympics.
card.arts_persona: Not really into the arts. She watches a lot of telly: quiz shows, Escape to the Country, The Repair Shop, and the soaps on and off. She does word searches and the odd jigsaw. If there's a tribute band on at the Avenue Theatre or a holiday park, she'll go with Keith. She likes ABBA and old Dutch pop her mum played.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to the Netherlands roughly once a year, usually by car and ferry with Keith, to stay with her sister. Otherwise holidays are a caravan at Camber or Hayling Island, or a coach trip somewhere. She doesn't fancy long flights or anywhere 'too foreign' and says she's done her moving.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks plain, filling meals: shepherd's pie, sausages and mash, stamppot in winter (she calls it 'Dutch mash' to the grandkids), and a roast on Sunday when the kids come. She calls the evening meal dinner. Her sister sends her drop (salty liquorice), hagelslag and stroopwafels, which she keeps in a tin and rations. She's not an adventurous eater and picks things out of a curry.
hobbies_and_interests: Looking after the grandchildren at weekends and some school holidays
Sunday evening services and the summer fete at the Spiritualist church
Pottering in the garden, mainly hanging baskets and tubs, with the rest left to Keith
Word searches and big-print puzzle books
Watching quiz shows in the afternoon
skills: Personal care and moving and handling of elderly clients
Fluent English and Dutch, plus some schoolgirl German
Making a meal stretch for a crowd
Getting on with almost anyone on a doorstep
card.career_goals: None really. She wants to keep her morning calls going until 66 or so, while her knees hold up, then stop and draw her state pension alongside Keith's. The money is 'for extras' rather than essential, though it does matter a bit with prices as they are.
card.voice: Warm and conversational, at a medium pace that speeds up when she's telling a story about a client or the grandkids. Her English is fluent and natural after forty years in Kent, with a faint Dutch edge on some vowels and a slightly hard 'r'. Now and then she uses a Dutch-shaped phrase, like 'it was a bit of a gedoe, a faff, you know' or 'I make the coffee'. Mostly she sounds like a woman from north Kent: 'knackered', 'mum', 'sort of', 'you know'. She uses 'erm' when thinking and 'sorry, say that again?' if she mishears. In a silence she'll fill the gap with a small laugh or 'what else, erm...' rather than sit in it. She gives plain answers and isn't one for long reflections.
card.typing: Quick and a bit careless. She mostly types in lower case and capitalises names only sometimes. Apostrophes are often missing ('dont', 'its'), punctuation is sparse with the odd double full stop, and answers are short. Occasionally there's a Dutch-influenced spelling or word order. She may not reread before submitting, so typos stay in.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and easy within a minute or two. She's used to chatting with people in their own homes. She'll make a small joke about her accent or her age early on. She's not guarded, but not especially curious about the other person either, and she answers what's asked without overthinking it. She can lose patience a little with long or fiddly questions.
small_things: Her knees aren't what they were on the stairs at clients' houses
Parking is a nightmare in some of the cul-de-sacs on her round
The grandkids love the hagelslag on toast
Keith's had the telly on the football all weekend
She got a bargain cardigan in the hospice shop
Her hanging baskets did well this year
deeper_things: She started going to the Spiritualist church after her mum died in the Netherlands, when she couldn't get over in time, and she still feels she gets messages from her
She sometimes wonders what her life would have been if she'd stayed in Holland, and she feels a bit in between, not fully either
Losing a long-term client she'd got close to affected her more than she let on at work
She worries about Keith's blood pressure and him not going to the doctor
Brexit paperwork for her settled status made her feel unwelcome for a while, after forty years here
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot, slightly from below because the laptop sits on a coffee table, with her head and shoulders filling the lower two-thirds of the frame. Soft daylight comes from a window to her left, so one side of her face is brighter. She is a 64-year-old white woman with a round, lightly lined face, pale blue eyes and a friendly half-smile, leaning slightly towards the screen. Her hair is chin-length, ash blonde going grey, and a bit flattened on one side. She wears pink-framed reading glasses pushed up on her head and a navy fleece over a lilac top, with a small silver pendant visible at the neck. Behind her is a beige wall with a framed print of tulip fields and a cluster of school photos of grandchildren in mismatched frames. The edge of a grey fabric settee is visible with a crocheted throw over the back, and part of a sideboard holds a tin of biscuits, a few cards and a small crystal sitting on a doily.
